questions.question: Which of the following is the rod-shaped structure found in the nucleus only when the cell is about to divide?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chromosomes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Chromosomes are rod-shaped structures that become visible during cell division.
 
• They are composed of DNA and proteins and carry genetic information.
 
• Chromosomes ensure that DNA is accurately replicated and distributed during cell division.
 
• Each species has a characteristic number of chromosomes; for humans, it's 46.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chromatin:**

 
 
• Chromatin is a complex of DNA and protein found in the nucleus, which condenses to form chromosomes during cell division.
 
• In its uncondensed form, chromatin is involved in gene expression and DNA replication.
 
 
 
• **Mitosis:**
 
 
• Mitosis is the process of cell division that results in two daughter cells with the same number of chromosomes as the parent cell.
 
• It involves stages such as prophase, metaphase, anaphase, and telophase.
 
 
 
• **Meiosis:**
 
 
• Meiosis is a type of cell division that reduces the chromosome number by half, resulting in four daughter cells, each with half the number of chromosomes of the parent cell.
 
• It is essential for sexual reproduction and genetic diversity.
 
 
 
• **Genome:**
 
 
• The genome is the complete set of genes or genetic material present in a cell or organism.
 
• In humans, the genome is organized into 23 pairs of chromosomes.

questions.question: What is the jelly like substance between the nucleus and the cell membrane called?
questions.solution: The correct answer is __**Cytoplasm**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** • Cytoplasm • **Cytoplasm** is the jelly - like substance present inside the cell. • It is jelly - like, because of its semi permeable characteristic. • It exists within the cell membrane. • Cytoplasm is extranuclear that means it does not exist within the cell’s nucleus.

questions.question: Where will you find plastids in a leaf cell?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**cytoplasm**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cytoplasm**:-

 
 
• **Cytoplasm is the jelly-like substance that fills the inside of a cell. **
 
• It is composed of water, salts, and various organic molecules, including proteins, carbohydrates, and lipids.
 
• Cytoplasm also contains organelles, which are specialized structures that perform specific functions within the cell.
 
• **Plastids are found in the cytoplasm of leaf cells.**
 
• They are typically located in the mesophyll cells, which are the cells in the middle of the leaf blade. Mesophyll cells are specialized for photosynthesis, and plastids are the organelles where photosynthesis takes place.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Cell Membrane:-**

 
 
• It is also known as the plasma membrane, is a thin, flexible barrier that surrounds all cells.
 
• **It is made up of a double layer of phospholipids, which are molecules that have a hydrophilic (water-loving) head and a hydrophobic (water-fearing) tail.**
 
 
 
• **Nucleus:-**
 
 
• **The nucleus is the control center of the cell. **
 
• It is a spherical organelle that is surrounded by a double membrane.
 
• The nucleus contains the cell's genetic material, which is organized into chromosomes.
 
 
 
• **Cell Wall:-**
 
 
• **A cell wall is a rigid, external layer that surrounds some types of cells, just outside the cell membrane. **
 
• It can be tough, flexible, and sometimes rigid.
 
• It provides the cell with both structural support and protection, and also acts as a filtering mechanism.

questions.question: Which of the following plant cells have large membranous organelles that help in photosynthesis?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Plastids**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Plastids** are large membranous organelles found in plant cells and some algae.
 
• They are primarily responsible for **photosynthesis**, which is the process by which plants convert light energy into chemical energy.
 
• Plastids contain the pigment **chlorophyll**, which is essential for capturing light energy.
 
• They also play a role in the synthesis and storage of food by the plant.
 
• Plastids can differentiate into various forms, such as **chloroplasts, chromoplasts,** and **leucoplasts**, depending on their function and the needs of the plant.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chloroplasts:** A type of plastid that contains chlorophyll and is the site of photosynthesis in plant cells.
 
• **Chromoplasts:** Plastids responsible for pigment synthesis and storage, giving colors to fruits and flowers.
 
• **Leucoplasts:** Non-pigmented plastids involved in the synthesis and storage of starch, oils, and proteins.
 
• **Thylakoids:** Membranous structures within chloroplasts where the light-dependent reactions of photosynthesis take place.
 
• **Stroma:** The fluid-filled space surrounding thylakoids in chloroplasts, where the Calvin cycle (light-independent reactions) occurs.

questions.question: In the division of the division, a parent cell is divided into _____________ for the preparation of mass cells.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Two Similar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• During cell division, a parent cell divides to form two similar daughter cells.
 
• This process ensures that each **daughter cell receives an identical set of genetic material** from the parent cell.
 
• Cell division is crucial for growth, repair, and reproduction in living organisms.
 
• There are two main types of cell division: **mitosis and meiosis**.
 
• Mitosis results in two identical daughter cells, while meiosis results in four genetically diverse cells.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mitosis**

 
 
• It is a type of cell division that results in two daughter cells each having the same number and kind of chromosomes as the parent nucleus.
 
• Mitosis is essential for growth and repair in multicellular organisms.
 
• It consists of several stages: **prophase, metaphase, anaphase, and telophase**.
 
 
 
• **Meiosis**
 
 
• Meiosis is a specialized form of cell division that reduces the chromosome number by half, resulting in four daughter cells, each genetically distinct from the parent cell.
 
• It is crucial for sexual reproduction and genetic diversity.
 
• Meiosis consists of two consecutive divisions: **meiosis I and meiosis II**.

questions.question: The organisms with cells having nuclear material without nuclear membrane are called as which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Prokaryotes .**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Prokaryotes** are creatures without a **nucleus or other organelles** in their cells.
 
• Prokaryotes differ from **eukaryotes** by not having** internal membranes.**
 
• **Bacteria and archaea,** which are considered to have** separate evolutionary lineages**, are the two main categories of prokaryotes.
 
• Prokaryotic cells include organisms like** cyanobacteria, E. coli, mycoplasma, etc. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Eukaryotes:**

 
 
• **Any cell or creature **with a **distinct nucleus **is said to be eukaryote.
 
• The nucleus, which houses the clearly delineated chromosomes, is **encased in a nuclear membrane** in eukaryotic cells.
 
 
 
• **Vacuoles:**
 
 
• **A membrane-bound cell organelle** known as a vacuole.
 
• **Animal cells** typically have tiny vacuoles that aid in the** sequestration of waste.**
 
• **Vacuoles in plant cells aid** in preserving the equilibrium of water.
 
 
 
• **Organelles:**
 
 
• It is a** tiny, membrane-enclosed structure** in a cell that serves a specific purpose.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:

1. Eukaryotic cells are cells without a nucleus and are found in single-celled organisms.

2. Prokaryotic cells are cells that contain a nucleus and they are found mainly in multicellular organisms.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Neither 1 nor 2**__.

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

​**Statement 1: Eukaryotic cells are cells without a nucleus and are found in single-celled organisms **

 
• Eukaryotic cells are cells that contain a nucleus.
 
• Eukaryotic cells are usually larger than prokaryotic cells, and they are found mainly in multicellular organisms.** Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.**
 
• Eukaryotic cells also contain other organelles besides the nucleus.
 
• Eukaryotic cells have a nucleus enclosed within the nuclear membrane and form large and complex organisms.
 
• They can maintain different environments in a single cell that allows them to carry out various metabolic reactions.
 
• This helps them grow many times larger than the prokaryotic cells. 
 
• Since eukaryotic cells typically have multiple linear chromosomes, capped with telomeres, eukaryotic DNA replication and cell division (mitosis and meiosis) are a bit more complicated.
 
• Protozoa, fungi, plants, and animals all have eukaryotic cells.

**Statement 2: Prokaryotic cells are cells that contain a nucleus and they are found mainly in multicellular organisms.**

 
• Prokaryotic cells are cells without a nucleus.
 
• Prokaryotic cells are found in single-celled organisms, such as **bacteria**. *Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.*
 
• Organisms with prokaryotic cells are called **prokaryotes**.
 
• They were the first type of organisms to evolve and are still the most common organisms today.
 
• Organisms that lack a membrane-bound nucleus are called prokaryotes.
 
• A prokaryotic cell does not contain a well-defined nucleus.
 
• The DNA in prokaryotic cells is in the cytoplasm rather than enclosed within a nuclear membrane.
 
• The genetic material is present on a single chromosome.
 
• All prokaryotes have a cell wall surrounding the cell membrane except in mycoplasma.
 
• The nucleolus is absent in prokaryotic cells.
 
• The fluid matrix filling the prokaryotic cell is the cytoplasm.
 
• Membrane-bound cell organelles are absent in prokaryotes.
 
• In prokaryotes, cell division takes place by fission or budding.
 
• Blue-green algae, bacteria, and mycoplasma are examples of prokaryotes.

questions.question: The presence of the cell wall enables the cells of plants, fungi and bacteria to exist without bursting in which medium?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hypotonic**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The presence of the cell wall enables the cells of plants, fungi and bacteria to exist in hypotonic media without bursting**__.

 __
 
• If the medium surrounding the cell has a higher water concentration than the cell, meaning that the outside solution is very dilute, the cell will gain water by osmosis.
 
• Such a solution is known as a hypotonic solution.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Isotonic:** If the medium has exactly the same water concentration as the cell, there will be no net movement of water across the cell membrane. Such a solution is known as an** isotonic solution**.
 
• **Hypertonic:** If the medium has a lower concentration of water than the cell, meaning that it is a very concentrated solution, the cell will lose water by osmosis. Such a solution is known as a **hypertonic solution**.

questions.question: Identify an organelle found both in eukaryotic as well as prokaryotic.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ribosomes**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ribosomes** are the only organelles found in both eukaryotic and prokaryotic cells.
 
• They are responsible for protein synthesis in the cell.
 
• Ribosomes can be found floating freely within the cytoplasm or attached to the endoplasmic reticulum in eukaryotic cells.
 
• In prokaryotic cells, ribosomes are smaller (70S) compared to those in eukaryotic cells (80S).
 
• Despite the size difference, the fundamental function of ribosomes remains the same across both cell types.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Prokaryotic cells** do not have membrane-bound organelles, which distinguishes them from eukaryotic cells.
 
• **Eukaryotic cells** contain various membrane-bound organelles, including the nucleus, mitochondria, and lysosomes, which are absent in prokaryotic cells.
 
• The presence of ribosomes in both cell types highlights their essential role in the fundamental process of protein synthesis.
 
• The differences in ribosome size between prokaryotes and eukaryotes are due to variations in their ribosomal RNA and protein content.

questions.question: The proteins and lipids, essential for building the cell membrane, are manufactured by
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**endoplasmic reticulum**__.

__**Explanation:**__

**Endoplasmic reticulum**

__
 
• Endoplasmic reticulum (ER) is an **extensive network of membrane-enclosed tubules **and cisternae located near the nucleus and golgi apparatus.
 
• It is **exclusively present in a eukaryotic cell. **
 
• Endoplasmic reticulum is a **large and dynamic structure** continuously **involved in protein synthesis, calcium storage and lipid metabolism.**__
 
• **Based on the presence or absence of ribosomes**, endoplasmic reticulum may either be **rough endoplasmic reticulum and smooth endoplasmic reticulum.**
 
• **Smooth endoplasmic reticulum (SER): **
 __
 
• These are smooth because they **do not bear ribosomes** on their surface.
 
• It is present in cells where they act as a **major site for the synthesis of lipids.**__
 
 
 
• **Rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER):**
 __
 
• They have rough membranes because they **bear ribosomes** attached to their surfaces.
 
• They are actively being seen in the cells which have their** involvement in the synthesis and secretion of proteins.**__
 
 

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ce8bc14d916bae4bfdae4fa49ba546548f28a8381f7c554d094c6a0602c61ba2.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__****Golgi apparatus:**

 
• Golgi Apparatus is a** dark-stained reticular structure **located near the cell nucleus. 
 
• This was later found to be present in other cell types and named as Golgi apparatus or the Golgi complex.
 
• It is a **membrane-bound cell organelle consisting of a series of flattened membranous sacs **that look like stacked pouches called cisternae. 

**Plasma membrane:**

 
• It is the **innermost layer of the cell envelope.**
 
• It is semi-permeable in nature and is responsible for the interaction of the cell with the outside environment.
 
• It h**elps in the regulation of the exchange of specific materials** between the cytoplasm and extracellular material.

**Mitochondria:**

 
• Mitochondria are **membrane-bound cell organelles** that are required to eukaryotic cells for aerobic respiration.
 
• These are also known as the** powerhouse of the cell.**
 
• There are two membranes in a mitochondrion: the outer and inner membranes.
 
• Out of which outer membrane is smooth and forms the continuous boundary of the organelle.
 
• The inner membrane is semipermeable to some metabolites.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the cell cycle is FALSE?

options.text: Preparation of mitosis takes place in G2 phase.
In M phase, the cell grows physically larger and copies organelles.
In S phase, replication of DNA takes place.
In G1 phase, the cell grows physically larger and copies organelles.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**In the M phase, the cell grows physically larger and copies organelles**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The ordered sequence of events that occur in a cell in preparation for cell division is called the cell cycle.
 
• The cell cycle is divided into two phases:
 
 
• **Interphase**
 
• **M Phase**
 
 
 
• The M Phase represents the phase when the actual cell division occurs.
 
• The Interphase represents the phase between two successive M phases.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Interphase is divided into three further phases;
 
 
• **G1 Phase**
 
• **S Phase**
 
• **G2 Phase**
 
 
 
• **During the G1 phase, t**he cell is metabolically active and continuously grows but does not replicate its **DNA**. 
 
• S or Synthesis phase marks the period during which **DNA **synthesis or replication takes place
 
• **During the G2 phase, **proteins are synthesized in preparation for mitosis while cell growth continues.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/20b251078149172c1b03f7d779402e459bab2398e8560645f0902597c44ed91d.png]

questions.question: Which cell organelle is an overlapping membranous sac with ER-like thickness that helps in processing and packaging protein and lipid molecules, especially stable proteins?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Golgi apparatus.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**__**Golgi Apparatus:**__

__
 
• The Golgi apparatus has multiple names such as the **Golgi complex or Golgi body.**
 
• The name is given on the name of the scientist, who discovered the organelle, i.e. Camillo Golgi.
 
• It is **found in all the eukaryotic cells**, plants as well as animals.
 
• They are membrane-bound organelles present in the cytosol of the cell.
 
• The Golgi body comprises 5 to 8 cup-shaped, series of compartments known as **cisternae**. Cisternae is a flattened, disk-shaped, stacked pouches that make up the Golgi apparatus. A Golgi stack mostly contains 4 to 8 cisternae. However, ~60 cisternae are found in some protists. A mammalian cell contains ~40 to 100 stacks of cisternae.
 
• Animal cells generally contain around 10 to 20 Golgi stacks per cell, which are connected by tubular connections.
 
• Golgi complex is mostly found near the nucleus.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8a66665c8b7d6a84497438e44c0511f463d9d862ee49c9ea1be606ed25af9562.png] 

**Functions of Golgi Bodies:**__

 
• Its main function is the **packaging and secretion of proteins.** 
 
• It receives proteins from Endoplasmic Reticulum. It packages it into **membrane-bound vesicles**, which are then transported to various destinations, such as lysosomes, plasma membrane or secretion.
 
• They also take part in the** transport of lipids **and the formation of lysosomes.
 
• **Post-translational modification and enzymatic processing** occur near the membrane surface in Golgi bodies, e.g. phosphorylation, glycosylation, etc.
 
• Golgi apparatus is the site for the synthesis of various glycolipids, sphingomyelin, etc.
 
• In the plant cells,** complex polysaccharides of the cell wall** are synthesised in the Golgi apparatus.

questions.question: A basic event in protein synthesis is the creation of a/an ____.
questions.solution:
• A basic event in protein synthesis is the creation of a/an mRNA (Messenger Ribonucleic Acid) copy.
 
• The mRNA provides the template for the Genetic Code.
 
• A gene is used to build a protein using the following two step process i.e. Transcription and Translation.
 
• **Transcription:** It is the process by which DNA is copied to mRNA, which carries the information needed for protein synthesis.
 
• **Translation:** It is the process that takes the information passed from DNA as messenger RNA and turns it into a series of amino acids.

questions.question: Rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER) looks rough under the microscope because of the attachment of which one of the following cell organelles to its surface?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Ribosomes__**.

**__The endoplasmic reticulum(ER)__** is a complex **network of membrane-bound structure** which runs through the cytoplasm.

__
 
• Within the folds of the ER membranes, we can find **spaces** called **Cisternae**__.
 
• It is connected to both the outer nuclear membrane as well as a cell membrane.
 
• The membrane has the same structure as the plasma membrane but ribosomes do not have membranes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

ER is divided into two types **depending on the absence or **presence **of ribosome on its surface:**

__
 
• **Rough Endoplasmic reticulum (RER)__**: It is rough in appearance and is lined with ribosomes, hence, named the rough endoplasmic reticulum. It is the site of **protein synthesis**.
 
• **__Smooth Endoplasmic reticulum (SER)__**: It contains **no ribosomes** and hence is smooth in appearance. It helps in lipid and steroid synthesis.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

**Functions of endoplasmic reticulum:**

__
 
• The endoplasmic reticulum helps in the **intracellular and intercellular transport** of materials.

 
 
• It is the “**transport system__**” of the cell.
 
• It **transports chemicals** between cells and within cells.
 
 
 
• RER is the site of **protein **synthesis and **enzyme synthesis**.
 __
 
• It conjugates with the Golgi body and helps in the **formation of lysosomes**.
 
 
 
• SER helps in lipid synthesis and **detoxifying** many **drugs** and **poisons**.
 
• The cell membrane is generated with the help of proteins and lipids synthesized in the ER. The process is known as **membrane biogenesis__**.

questions.question: Which membrane-bound cell organelle consisting of a small sac-like structure surrounded by single membranes serves as the cell's digestive system, allowing material taken from outside the cell to degrade and digest obsolete components of the cell?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lysosome**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ​Lysosome:

 
 
• Lysosomes are an important cell organelle found within eukaryotic animal cells.
 
• Due to their peculiar function, they are also known as the “suicide bags” of the cell.
 
• Lysosomes work as the waste-discarding structures of the cell by processing undesirable materials and degrading them, both from the exterior of the cell and waste constituents inside the cell.
 
• But sometimes, the digestive enzymes may end up damaging the lysosomes themselves, and this can cause the cell to die.
 
• This is termed autolysis, where **“auto” means “self” and “lysis” means “the disintegration of the cell by the destruction of its cell membrane“**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Peroxisomes:

 
 
• It is a microbody.
 
• In-plant it helps in photorespiration.
 
• In animals concerned with peroxide metabolism.
 
 
 
• Glyoxysomes: These are the **special type of peroxisomes found in plants & some fungi.**
 
• **Polysome:** Many **ribosomes may associate with a single mRNA** to form **multiple copies of a polypeptide simultaneously**.
 
 
• Such strings of ribosomes are termed as **Polysome**.
